title: Hourly to Annual Salary: How to Use Home Loan Salary Sacrifice with Your Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary with our guide. Includes home loan salary sacrifice, casual loading, super, and tax for Australian workers.
salarySummary: For a full-time 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours times 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours and then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading to see the annual equivalent.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave and other entitlements. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees, but casual employees receive $33.05 per hour (including 25% loading). When using our timesheet, check the casual loading box to add 25% to your base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How does home loan salary sacrifice work with my salary?
faqs.a: Home loan salary sacrifice is an arrangement where your employer pays part of your salary directly towards your home loan, reducing your taxable income. This can lower the tax you pay and help you pay off your mortgage faster. However, our calculator does not include salary sacrifice – it assumes no salary sacrifice arrangements. For personalised advice, consult your employer or a tax professional. The Australian Taxation Office sets rules for salary sacrifice, and it may affect your super guarantee and other entitlements.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Conversion

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, super, and any deductions.

For example, if your base hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross pay would be $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual equivalent instantly.

### Casual Loading and Super

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to casual loading – an extra 25% on top of your base rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. For instance, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees, but casual employees receive $33.05 per hour (including 25% loading). When using our timesheet, check the casual loading box to add 25% to your base rate. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the checkbox adds it for you.

Superannuation (super) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at the super guarantee rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). Super is not deducted from your pay; your employer pays it separately. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. For example, on a $59,280 annual salary, your employer would contribute $7,113.60 in super. Our calculator estimates super based on ordinary earnings only, and it stops at the maximum base.

### Tax and Medicare

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners using 2025–26 thresholds (as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). Our calculator applies these rates but does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or any offsets.

### Home Loan Salary Sacrifice

Home loan salary sacrifice is an arrangement where your employer directs part of your pre-tax salary to your home loan, reducing your taxable income. This can lower your tax bill and help you pay off your mortgage faster. However, our calculator assumes no salary sacrifice – it shows your pay without any packaging. If you use home loan salary sacrifice, your taxable income will be lower, which may affect your tax, super, and other entitlements. The Australian Taxation Office regulates salary sacrifice, and it must be agreed with your employer. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) is the home page where you enter your base hourly rate. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top. The calculator then shows your annual gross pay, fortnightly pay (weekly × 2), estimated tax, Medicare, super, and take-home pay. It uses the assumptions above. Remember, this is an estimate – actual pay may vary due to penalties, allowances, or different hours.

For award-specific rates, see our [pay guides](/blog). For industry averages, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings: full-time adult ordinary time $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). All employees total earnings average $1,579.20 per week (includes part-time). These are averages, not medians for your specific job. For job-specific pay, see our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page.

### Important Notes

- Annual pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses 2026–27 resident rates with full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (2026–27 not confirmed).
- HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more reference tables, see our [reference tables](/data). For minimum wage details, see [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage). For take-home pay calculations, see [take-home pay](/topics/take-home). For hourly conversion methods, see [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion). For casual loading specifics, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).
